input.brief: Ahmed Wagdy, DevOps / Platform / MLOps engineer; AI gateways, GPU clusters, Kubernetes, CI security gates

direction.name: The printed annual
direction.idea: Lay the page out like a well-designed printed report or magazine feature: a masthead image, a tight oversized title, text held to a strict column line, and colour used in solid blocks the way a two-colour print job would. It gives weight and authority to subjects that are really about content: findings, a manifesto, a programme, a serious product. The reader should feel that someone edited this.
direction.composition: A fixed vertical axis at about 42% of the viewport width organises everything: headings begin on it, body columns hang from it, and the 0–42% zone holds small side notes, figures or stays empty. Masthead: a wide image band (photographic mosaic or a single crop) across the top 45% of the first screen; below it the title at 7–9vw starting on the axis, with a two-sentence standfirst at 20–24px. Sections alternate between text pages (title on the axis, body in one or two columns of 34–40ch to its right) and full-bleed colour pages carrying one large figure, quotation or image mosaic. Mosaics are gutterless: photographs and flat colour tiles butted together in a 4- or 6-cell grid. Page numbers, running heads and other print furniture are left out.
direction.typography: A tight heavy grotesk or a sharp serif for titles; an excellent text face for reading at 18–20px with leading near 1.5. Headings in sentence case, tracked tight.
direction.colour: Paper, ink and two or three solid block colours. A colour page is a whole section in one flat colour.
direction.imagery: Photographs used as blocks in mosaics alongside flat colour tiles; mixed subjects are fine if cropped tight and converted to one treatment.
direction.photoTreatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.
direction.richness: The column line, the mosaics and whole pages of colour give structure and variety without ornaments.
direction.pitfalls: The axis must be exact and reused everywhere or it reads as random indentation. Keep paragraphs to a real reading measure. On a phone the axis collapses to the left margin and side notes move inline above their paragraph.

hero.name: Narrow talk, wide headline
hero.blueprint: An asymmetric sheet on one flat paper-grey ground, divided at 34% of the width by alignment only. Left column (columns 1-4, 32px margin): the wordmark top-left; then, starting at 30% of the height, one supporting sentence at 22px with leading 1.35, max 24ch; under it the single action, a solid ink rectangle with square corners. The column's lower third is empty. Right column (columns 5-12): four text links at 15px on its top edge, the first aligned exactly to the 34% line. Beneath them the headline in a very heavy grotesk at clamp(88px, 9.8vw, 150px), two lines, line-height 0.82, tracking -0.04em, flush left on the 34% line and filling the column width. A square-cornered photograph the full width of the right column starts at 68% of the viewport height and is cropped by the bottom edge. A solid accent block 260px wide, carrying one real figure at 40px and one line of text, overlaps the photograph's top-left corner by half its own height using a negative top margin.
hero.mobile: One column on 20px margins. The wordmark and a menu word share the top row. The headline comes first at 15vw on two lines, heavy, line-height 0.85. The supporting sentence follows at 18px, then the action at full width. The photograph runs full bleed below at 4:3, with the accent block overlapping its top-left corner at 60% of the screen width.
hero.headline: A 2-4 word statement in the heaviest weight, at most 20 characters, one or two words per line.

type.note: A heavy, round old-style headline face with soft bracketed serifs over a clear transitional text serif. Suits essays, food, independent publishers and personal sites that want warmth with weight.

palette.name: Bottle ink, yellow
palette.note: Off-white ground with all type in a near-black bottle green instead of black. Yellow is the only saturated note: the button or one small object on most screens, and one later section that turns fully yellow.

photos.note: structure, lines, bridges, facades and building interiors
photos.treatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Bars standing on the edge
sections.blueprint: The product's own chart, drawn in HTML, is the whole section. A full-bleed field 90svh tall. Along its bottom edge stand ten to fourteen solid bars, one per true value (months, releases, cohorts), in a CSS grid spanning the full viewport width with 8px gaps and no side margins; heights are the values scaled so the tallest is 58vh. No axes, no grid, no legend; the chart's root is marked data-ui. Every bar is one tone two steps from the field except the one the page is about, which takes the accent. Three bars print their value directly above themselves at clamp(20px, 2vw, 30px), tabular. The headline figure sits top-left on the page margin at clamp(88px, 10vw, 168px), and its claim, two to five words at 28px, sits beneath it on the same margin. Hovering or focusing a bar shows its value and period above it.
sections.mobile: Bars run sideways: each a full-width row 28px tall growing from the left edge, 6px gaps, eight values at most. The headline figure sits above at 26vw with its claim at 22px. Three rows print their value at 17px inside the bar's right end. The accent row stays.

sections.name: Side facts, wide paragraph
sections.blueprint: Two rows share one vertical line at 34% of the viewport width. Row one: in a 160px column at the left margin, three label and value pairs stack with 20px between them, each a label in the soft ink with its value beneath in full ink, all at 13px (founded, based in, team size). From the 34% line a five-line paragraph at clamp(20px, 1.7vw, 26px), leading 1.35, runs to 90% of the width. Row two starts 120px lower and repeats the logic for the record of the practice: one plain word at 13px at the far left (awards, press, clients), then from the 34% line two list columns, each 260px wide with a 64px gutter, at 13px with 10px between lines: name at the left, year at the right in the soft ink. No heading; the paragraph opens the section. Each list comfortably holds 6–12 lines. No photographs are needed.
sections.mobile: Everything aligns to the left margin. The paragraph comes first at 19px. The three label and value pairs follow as a two-column grid at 14px. The two record lists stack with 40px between them, each opened by its plain word in full ink.

sections.name: One long letter
sections.blueprint: A single testimonial given room to be read, set like a letter. One column 34–38ch wide begins at column 5 of 12, or shares the page's own reading column. The first sentence of the quotation is pulled up as the opening line at 28–32px in medium weight, two lines at most. The rest follows as two or three ordinary paragraphs at 18–19px with leading 1.55 and 20px between paragraphs, in the full ink, not grey. It closes the way a letter does: 40px of space, then the name on one line and the role on the next at 16px. In columns 1–3, top-aligned with the first line, sits either nothing or one small square photograph of the writer, 120px wide. There are no quotation marks at all; the letter form makes them unnecessary. Space above and below is 140px.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 20px margins. If there is a photograph it goes first at 96px square, left-aligned. Opening sentence at 24px, body at 17px, sign-off beneath. Nothing else changes; this section is already a phone composition.

sections.name: Sentence, portrait, two links
sections.blueprint: One closing row of three elements hanging from the same top line, with open ground between them, on a 12-column grid. Columns 1–5: a sentence of 12–18 words at clamp(26px, 3vw, 44px), four lines, leading 1.1, saying what kind of enquiries are welcome; it is set as a paragraph and there is no separate heading. Columns 8–9: one small square portrait or photograph of the place, 150–170px, with square corners. Columns 10–12: a short question at 18px in medium weight, then 20px below it two underlined links stacked at 18px (the email address and one booking or social link), and beneath them a line at 14px in the soft ink with the city and the usual reply time. Columns 6–7 stay empty. The row has 160px of space above and 120px below. No form. On a dark ground the photograph is the only bright thing in the row.
sections.mobile: The sentence comes first at 7.4vw. Below it the portrait at 96px square sits at the left margin with the question and the two links to its right, top-aligned, in the remaining width. The city and reply-time line spans the full width beneath.

sections.name: Columns above, wordmark below
sections.blueprint: The footer inverts ground and ink and fills a whole viewport (min-height 100svh), arranged as three rows in a grid (auto 1fr auto). Top row, 40px from the edge: four small columns on the 12-column grid (address, navigation, social, hours or contact), each a plain list at 15–16px with its first line in the full ink and the rest in the softer ink. Middle row: empty. Bottom row: the wordmark alone, sized to run from the left margin to the right margin on one line. Set it as inline SVG text with a `viewBox` fitted to the word and `width: 100%`, or tune `font-size` in `vw` to the letter count, so it never wraps; its baseline sits 20px above a single line of legal text at 13px. With `position: sticky; bottom: 0` and a lower `z-index` than the page, the last section slides away to uncover it.
sections.mobile: Columns become two by two at 15px with 32px between rows, at the top. A gap of about 20svh follows. The wordmark spans the full width at the bottom; a name longer than ten letters stacks on two lines, each fitted to the width. Legal line beneath at 12px.

references.name: Applied Imagination
references.idea: An essay conceived on a flight is read as a descent: an altimeter ticks from 30,000 ft to zero while you scroll down through halftone clouds to mountains at ground level.
references.hero: A pale blue sky fading to warm cream fills the viewport, with white clouds shaded in halftone dots. A tiny serif logotype sits top-centre; no nav. The title, two centred lines of black wedge-serif at 8.9vw, occupies the middle half of the screen and about 73% of its width; a cloud layer passes in front of the second line's baseline so the feet of the letters dissolve into dots. A two-line centred deck at 24px sits beneath. A mono byline strip is centred on the bottom edge with a scroll cue bottom-right. On the left edge at mid-height, a short vertical rule carries a two-line mono altitude readout.
references.type: fsKim, a sturdy wedge-serif display face, regular weight at 128px with -0.01em tracking for the title and pull quotes; gtAmerica at 24px for the deck and about 16px for essay body; gtAmericaMono uppercase around 11px with wide tracking for byline, altitude and tape labels.
references.colour: #cbe4f2 #f1e3b5 #0a0a0a #ffc013 #8e2f8f #f04e23 — Sky blue melting into sand yellow is the constant ground and text is black. Saturated magenta, orange and yellow arrive only in collage objects, tape labels and the footer contact card.
references.imagery: Photo-collage cut-outs (parachutes carrying a treasure chest and a burning dumpster, a pair of legs, mountains) given a coarse halftone dot screen, layered in front of and behind the type against painted clouds.
references.layout: A narrow text column about 38% wide for essay passages, interrupted by full-width display pull quotes and collage objects floating at the edges. One continuous sky instead of sections, with a fixed left-edge altimeter. Nearly 23 screens, ending on a ground-level landscape.

sections.description: Sky background, no container. A three-line pull quote in black wedge-serif at about 7vw is centred and tightly leaded. Two cut-out parachutes hang over it: a magenta one from the top-left carrying a chest spilling coins, an orange one at lower right carrying a burning dumpster, each overlapping letterforms. Small mono labels on tilted strips of coloured tape are stuck to the objects. Words in the quote turn from grey to black as they are reached.

Running essay text in about 16px grotesk, black, in a single column roughly 38% of the viewport wide, positioned left of centre with large sky margins on both sides. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line; serif sub-statements at about 28px introduce passages. The next display quote is seen rising from below, its letters partly hidden behind cloud and blurred.

Ground level: halftone-screened mountains in green and brown rise from both sides, and the title returns at huge scale, cropped by the top edge and tucked behind the peaks. Centred below is a square-cornered two-panel card: a cream left panel with a short form of two fields and a small orange button, and a magenta right panel with a round portrait, name and a yellow subscribe button. Yellow tape-strip credits sit on the bottom edge.

steal: Tie a persistent numeric readout to scroll position (altitude falling to zero) so the reader's progress becomes part of the story.
Layer an illustration element in front of the bottom of a giant title so the letters sink into the scene instead of sitting on top.
Apply one coarse halftone dot screen to every photo cut-out so collage pieces from different sources read as one illustration set.

references.name: Architecture of Socialist-Era Belgrade
references.idea: A two-colour printed guidebook on screen: signal-red type over greyscale concrete, with one modular display face as the only ornament.
references.hero: Full-bleed greyscale photograph of brutalist housing towers; pale sky fills the top half, concrete the bottom. The title is set over the sky, flush left at a 32px margin, three lines in a wide modular display face at 102px (7.1vw) in flat red, the longest line reaching 92% of the width, leading so tight that the lines almost touch. Under it, one row at 24px: a red one-line descriptor at left, and two paler-red facts right-aligned (an object count and a date range). Top-right, the word 'Index' with a diagonal arrow. No logo, no button, nothing else. Red and grey only.
references.type: IntraNet, a wide modular display face with rounded, notched corners, used only for the title and its footer repeat. Funnel Sans carries the rest: about 50px for the long intro, 40px bold uppercase entry titles, 24px meta, 13px credits. Four sizes, two faces.
references.colour: #f53843 #d1d1d1 #c7c7c7 #777777 #f1a7ab — Strictly red and grey: red text on grey photo or grey paper, then pale grey text on a solid red field for the essay and footer. Photographs are desaturated so nothing breaks the pair.
references.imagery: Contemporary black-and-white architectural photographs of concrete towers and complexes, frontal or looking up, with big skies and visible grain; full-bleed in the hero, full column width and square-cornered in entries.
references.layout: 16 to 32px margins, everything flush left. A long red essay block in very large text, then twenty repeated entry blocks on grey: a two-column header split by a vertical red hairline, a meta row, then a wide photo. 81 screens of the same rhythm.

sections.description: Immediately under the hero photo a solid red field begins with no gap. The essay runs as one full-width column in pale grey sans at roughly 50px with tight leading, about 50 characters per line, paragraphs separated by one blank line, with no headings, pull-quotes or images for several screens. The photo's bottom edge butts straight against the red.

Each building entry sits on light grey paper: a thin red rule across the top, then two columns divided by a vertical red hairline at the 50% mark. Left: the building's name in red bold uppercase at 40px over two lines. Right: its dates in pale red at the same size. Below, a small meta row with 'Credits' and 'Address' labels and values in 13px red, then a full-width greyscale photograph.

Solid red. At the top, two short 13px notes side by side in pale grey occupy the left 60%, a back-to-top link sits far right, and a third note runs beneath. A tall empty red gap follows. Then the full title is repeated in the display face at hero size but in pale grey, flush left, above a single row of small meta: sources link left, font credits centre, city and year right.

steal: Limit the page to one saturated colour and one grey, desaturate all photos, and invert the pair (grey on red) for long reading blocks.
Set the title in a distinctive modular display face directly on the sky area of a photo and repeat it in the footer in the inverse colour.
Put facts in the hero as a right-aligned row of paler-tint figures (count, date range) on the same baseline as the subtitle.

references.name: Dabbit
references.idea: The colour picker demonstrates itself on the page: its loupe sits in the hero reading the site's own background hex, and every feature is shown as a real fragment of the app.
references.hero: Near-black viewport split exactly in half by a one-pixel vertical hairline. Left half: a small chrome four-petal logo top-left at a 40px margin, then two thirds of empty dark, then everything else anchored bottom-left: a one-line 30px medium-weight headline, three lines of grey 18px copy, a light pill button beside an outlined pill, and a tiny note. Right half: a 450px rounded square with a thin iridescent border, the app's loupe, empty except for a centre crosshair dot and a small chip reading the hex of the page's own background. Eight pastel dots and lozenges drift across the top-right like spilled swatches.
references.type: InterVariable only. Headline a modest 30px medium with -0.025em tracking; section heads about 22px; cell titles 15px; body 16px grey. Largest text is 3.3vw. Hierarchy comes from white against grey rather than size; hex values use tabular figures.
references.colour: #141416 #2b2b2e #f4f3f2 #9a9aa0 #f4a48c #d4c6e6 — Charcoal ground, off-white and grey text, no brand accent. All colour comes from the product: pastel swatches, tonal scales, and a thin prismatic edge on the loupe and logo. Neutral-cool.
references.imagery: Live-drawn UI fragments on canvas: swatch strips, eleven-step scales, contrast tables, a Figma plugin panel, each in a slightly lighter rounded panel. A chrome 3D logo and chrome price numerals are the only non-UI images.
references.layout: 40px outer margins; the hero's centre hairline becomes a three-column then four-column hairline grid. No section changes background; rhythm is small eyebrow, heading, grid, repeat. Text sits top-left in every cell.

sections.description: A three-column grid ruled by one-pixel hairlines with no card backgrounds. Each cell is over 400px tall: 15px white title and three lines of grey copy, plus a real UI fragment docked above or below (a swatch history strip, a tonal scale, a contrast table, a ten-by-ten colour matrix). Rows alternate text-over-mock and mock-over-text so the grid staggers. The loupe square from the hero reappears floating across cell boundaries.

A four-column, three-row grid of minor features divided by hairlines. Each item is a 14px title prefixed by a tiny coloured glyph (dot, square, triangle or dash, one shape per column, in the app's pastel colours) and two lines of grey text. No icons, no cards, no hover chrome.

Left third: small grey eyebrow, a 22px heading, one paragraph. Right: the price rendered as huge chrome 3D numerals about 150px tall with the loupe square overlapping them, a tiny qualifier beside, and a plain four-line checklist beneath. No pricing card, no border, no tiers.

Closing block centred on the same dark ground: the chrome four-petal logo enlarged to about 200px, pastel shapes scattered widely around it, a two-line 22px sentence, the same two pill buttons, then a one-line footer with copyright left and seven text links right.

steal: Make the hero demo sample the page itself: the tool reports the site's own background value, proving the product without a screenshot.
Build feature grids from hairlines and real UI fragments instead of bordered cards and icons, alternating text-above and mock-above per row.
Keep the headline small (30px) and anchored bottom-left so the product object, not the slogan, owns the first viewport.
